digoxin.considerations: Base the dose on lean body weight and corrected CrCl, then adjust to clinical response and serum digoxin concentrations. Steady state takes 7–19 days depending on renal function.

tables.indication: Loading dose, if needed (adults) · US label Table 1

rows.dose: 10–15 mcg/kg in total: half first, then ¼ every 6–8 h twice, assessing response and toxicity before each dose

ckd.notes: Corrected CrCl is per 70 kg or 1.73 m²; the label estimates it in men as (140 − age) ÷ SCr, × 0.85 in women. * = about 30% below the calculated dose: check a level and increase if needed. Alternative: maintenance = loading dose × (14 + CrCl/5) ÷ 100. Reduce the dose when lean weight is a small fraction of total body mass (obesity, oedema). Levels <0.5 ng/mL are associated with diminished efficacy and >2 ng/mL with toxicity; adverse reactions may increase above 1.2 ng/mL. Doses come from studies in heart failure.
ev: Table 3 provides the recommended (once daily) maintenance dose for adults and pediatric patients over 10 years old (to be given once daily) according to lean body weight and renal function
Recommended doses approximately 30 percent lower than the calculated dose are designated with an *
Total Maintenance Dose = Loading Dose (i.e., Peak Body Stores) x % Daily Loss/100 (% Daily Loss = 14 + Creatinine clearance/5)
Serum digoxin levels less than 0.5 ng/mL have been associated with diminished efficacy, while levels above 2 ng/mL have been associated with increased toxicity without increased benefit
As digoxin serum levels increase above 1.2 ng/mL, there is a potential for increase in adverse reactions

ihd.notes: Not removed by dialysis: give no supplement after haemodialysis. The label dose table stops at CrCl 10 mL/min, so the maintenance dose in dialysis patients is individualised from serum levels (half-life 3.5–5 days in anuria).
ev: Digoxin is not effectively removed from the body by dialysis, exchange transfusion, or during cardiopulmonary bypass because most of the drug is bound to extravascular tissues
The half-life in anuric patients is prolonged to 3.5-5 days

pd.notes: The label states digoxin is not effectively removed by dialysis (modality not specified). No PD dose is given; individualise from serum levels.
ev: Digoxin is not effectively removed from the body by dialysis because of its large extravascular volume of distribution

halfLife.ev: In healthy volunteers with normal renal function, digoxin has a half-life of 1.5-2 days

renalHalfLife.ev: The half-life in anuric patients is prolonged to 3.5-5 days

volumeOfDistribution.ev: Digoxin is concentrated in tissues and therefore has a large apparent volume of distribution (approximately 475-500 L)

proteinBinding.ev: Approximately 25% of digoxin in the plasma is bound to protein
